tools.name: describe_table
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific table

tableId.description: The ID or name of the table

detailLevel.description:
Detail level for table information:
- tableIdentifiersOnly: table IDs and names
- identifiersOnly: table, field, and view IDs and names
- full: complete details including field types, descriptions, and configurations

Note for LLMs: To optimize context window usage, request the minimum detail level needed:
- Use 'tableIdentifiersOnly' when you only need to list or reference tables
- Use 'identifiersOnly' when you need to work with field or view references
- Only use 'full' when you need field types, descriptions, or other detailed configuration

If you only need detailed information on a few tables in a base with many complex tables, it might be more efficient for you to use list_tables with tableIdentifiersOnly, then describe_table with full on the specific tables you want.

tools.description: Upload a file directly to an attachment field on an existing record using Airtable's upload API. Supports files up to 5 MB. For larger files, use create_record or update_records with a public URL. The record must already exist.

recordId.description: The ID of the existing record (e.g. recXXXXXXXXXXXXXX)

attachmentFieldIdOrName.description: The ID or name of the attachment field (e.g. fldXXXXXXXXXXXXXX or "Images")

file.description: Raw base64-encoded file content (no data URL prefix)

tools.name: confluence_add_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a Confluence page.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to add a comment to

body.description: The comment content in Markdown format

tools.name: confluence_add_inline_comment
tools.description: Add an inline comment anchored to a text selection on a page.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to add the inline comment to

body.description: The comment content in Markdown format

text_selection.description: The exact text on the page to anchor the inline comment to. Must match text that exists in the page content.

text_selection_match_count.description: Total number of times the selected text appears on the page. Defaults to 1.

text_selection_match_index.description: Zero-based index of which occurrence of the text to anchor to. Defaults to 0 (first occurrence).

tools.name: confluence_add_label
tools.description:
Add label to Confluence content (pages, blog posts, or attachments).

Useful for:
- Categorizing attachments (e.g., 'screenshot', 'diagram', 'legal-doc')
- Tracking status (e.g., 'approved', 'needs-review', 'archived')
- Filtering content by topic or version

page_id.description: Confluence content ID to label. For pages/blogs: numeric ID (e.g., '123456789'). For attachments: ID with 'att' prefix (e.g., 'att123456789'). Use get_attachments to find attachment IDs.

name.description: Label name to add (lowercase, no spaces). Examples: 'draft', 'reviewed', 'confidential', 'v1.0'. Labels help organize and categorize content.

tools.name: confluence_check_content_permissions
tools.description:
Check whether a user or group can perform an operation on specific content.

Wraps POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/permission/check.

Note: This tool is only available for Confluence Cloud. Server/Data Center
instances use different permission APIs.

Returns a JSON object with a 'hasPermission' boolean indicating whether
the subject has the requested permission on the content.

content_id.description: Confluence content ID (page, blog post, comment, or attachment). Example: '123456789'

user_identifier.description: Account ID of the user (for subject_type='user') or group ID (for subject_type='group'). Example user account ID: '5b10a2844c20165700ede21g'

operation.description: The operation to check. Common values: 'read', 'update', 'delete', 'export', 'purge', 'administer', 'create_or_delete_from_view'.

subject_type.description: Whether the subject is a 'user' or a 'group'. Defaults to 'user'.

tools.name: confluence_copy_page
tools.description:
Copy a Confluence page to a new location.

On Confluence Cloud the native copy endpoint is used.  On Server/Data Center
the page body is fetched and a new page is created manually (attachments are
not copied in the Server/DC path).

source_page_id.description: The ID of the page to copy

destination_space_key.description: Space key for the new page (e.g. 'DEV', 'TEAM')

new_title.description: Title for the new copied page

destination_parent_id.description: (Optional) Parent page ID in the destination space. When omitted the page is created at the space root.

copy_attachments.description: (Optional) Whether to copy attachments to the new page. Defaults to true. Only supported on Confluence Cloud.

tools.name: confluence_create_page
tools.description: Create a new Confluence page.

space_key.description: The key of the space to create the page in (usually a short uppercase code like 'DEV', 'TEAM', or 'DOC')

content.description: The content of the page. Format depends on content_format parameter. Can be Markdown (default), wiki markup, storage format, or XHTML storage format. Either 'content' or 'content_file' must be provided, but not both.

parent_id.description: (Optional) parent page ID. If provided, this page will be created as a child of the specified page

content_format.description: (Optional) The format of the content parameter. Options: 'markdown' (default), 'wiki', 'storage', or 'xhtml'. Use 'xhtml' when providing Confluence XHTML storage format (same as 'storage'). Wiki format uses Confluence wiki markup syntax

enable_heading_anchors.description: (Optional) Whether to enable automatic heading anchor generation. Only applies when content_format is 'markdown'

include_content.description: (Optional) Whether to include page content in the response. Defaults to false since callers already have the content at create time

emoji.description: (Optional) Page title emoji (icon shown in navigation). Can be any emoji character like '📝', '🚀', '📚'. Set to null/None to remove.

content_file.description: (Optional) Absolute or relative filesystem path to read the page body from (UTF-8). Use this instead of 'content' when the body is too large to pass comfortably as a tool argument. Mutually exclusive with 'content'.

page_width.description: (Optional) Page layout width. Options: 'full-width', 'default'. Defaults to null (Confluence default).

table_layout.description: (Optional) Table width preset applied to all markdown tables. Options: 'full-width' (1800 px), 'wide' (960 px), 'default' (760 px). Only applies when content_format is 'markdown'.

subtype.description: (Optional) Confluence page subtype. Use 'live' to create a Confluence Live Doc. Only supported for Confluence Cloud.

tools.name: confluence_create_page_from_template
tools.description:
Create a new Cloud page pre-populated with a template's body.

This operation is only available for Confluence Cloud.
Fetches the named template and creates a page with its storage-format
content.  The page can be edited afterwards via confluence_update_page.

space_key.description: Key of the space in which to create the page.

template_id.description: ID of the template to use as the page body.

parent_id.description: Optional ID of the parent page.

tools.name: confluence_delete_attachment
tools.description:
Permanently delete an attachment from Confluence.

**Warning**: This action cannot be undone! The attachment and ALL its versions will be
permanently deleted.

Use this tool to:
- Remove outdated or incorrect attachments
- Clean up duplicate files
- Delete sensitive information that was accidentally uploaded

Best practices:
- Verify the attachment ID before deletion using get_attachments
- Consider downloading the attachment first as a backup
- Check with content owners before deleting shared attachments

attachment_id.description: The ID of the attachment to delete. Attachment IDs can be found using the get_attachments tool. Example: 'att123456789'. **Warning**: This permanently deletes the attachment and all its versions.

tools.name: confluence_delete_page
tools.description: Delete an existing Confluence page.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to delete

tools.name: confluence_download_attachment
tools.description:
Download an attachment from Confluence as an embedded resource.

Returns the attachment content as a base64-encoded embedded resource so
that it is available over the MCP protocol without requiring filesystem
access on the server. Files larger than 50 MB are not downloaded inline;
a descriptive error message is returned instead.

attachment_id.description: The ID of the attachment to download (e.g., 'att123456789'). Find attachment IDs using get_attachments tool. Example workflow: get_attachments(content_id) → use returned ID here.

tools.name: confluence_download_content_attachments
tools.description:
Download all attachments for a Confluence content item as embedded resources.

Returns attachment contents as base64-encoded embedded resources so that
they are available over the MCP protocol without requiring filesystem
access on the server. Files larger than 50 MB are skipped with an error
entry in the summary.

content_id.description: The ID of the Confluence content (page or blog post) to download attachments from. Example: '123456789'

tools.name: confluence_get_attachments
tools.description:
List all attachments for a Confluence content item (page or blog post).

Returns metadata about attachments including:
- Attachment ID, title, and file type
- File size and download URL
- Creation/modification dates
- Version information

**Important**: Confluence API returns 'application/octet-stream' as the media type
for most binary files (PNG, JPG, PDF) instead of specific types like 'image/png'.
For filtering by file type, using the 'filename' parameter is more reliable
(e.g., filename='*.png' pattern matching if supported, or exact filename).

Useful for:
- Discovering what files are attached to a page
- Getting attachment IDs for download operations
- Checking if a specific file exists
- Listing images/documents for processing

content_id.description: The ID of the Confluence content (page or blog post) to list attachments for. Example: '123456789'

start.description: (Optional) Starting index for pagination. Use 0 for the first page. To get the next page, add the 'limit' value to 'start'. Default: 0

limit.description: (Optional) Maximum number of attachments to return per request (1-100). Use pagination (start/limit) for large attachment lists. Default: 50

filename.description: (Optional) Filter results to only attachments matching this filename. Exact match only. Example: 'report.pdf'

media_type.description: (Optional) Filter by MIME type. **Note**: Confluence API returns 'application/octet-stream' for most binary files (PNG, JPG, PDF) instead of specific MIME types like 'image/png'. For more reliable filtering, use the 'filename' parameter. Examples: 'application/octet-stream' (binary files), 'application/pdf', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document' (for .docx)

tools.name: confluence_get_comments
tools.description: Get comments for a specific Confluence page.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be parsed from URL, e.g. from 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title' -> '123456789')

tools.name: confluence_get_inline_comments
tools.description: Get all inline comments for a Confluence page.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to get inline comments from

tools.name: confluence_get_labels
tools.description: Get labels for Confluence content (pages, blog posts, or attachments).

page_id.description: Confluence content ID (page, blog post, or attachment). For pages: numeric ID from URL (e.g., '123456789'). For attachments: ID with 'att' prefix (e.g., 'att123456789'). Works with any Confluence content type that supports labels.

tools.name: confluence_get_page
tools.description: Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID, full page URL, or tiny link. For example: '123456789', 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', or 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/x/N4CIO'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

tools.name: confluence_get_page_children
tools.description: Get child pages and folders of a specific Confluence page.

parent_id.description: The ID of the parent page whose children you want to retrieve

expand.description: Fields to expand in the response (e.g., 'version', 'body.storage')

limit.description: Maximum number of child items to return (1-50)

include_content.description: Whether to include the page content in the response

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page content to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Only relevant if include_content is true.

include_folders.description: Whether to include child folders in addition to child pages

tools.name: confluence_get_page_diff
tools.description: Get a unified diff between two versions of a Confluence page.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'.

tools.name: confluence_get_page_history
tools.description: Get a historical version of a specific Confluence page.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'.

version.description: The version number of the page to retrieve

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

tools.name: confluence_get_page_images
tools.description:
Get all images attached to a Confluence page as inline image content.

Filters attachments to images only (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG, BMP)
and returns them as base64-encoded ImageContent that clients can
render directly. Non-image attachments are excluded.

Files with ambiguous MIME types (application/octet-stream) are
detected by filename extension as a fallback. Images larger than
50 MB are skipped with an error entry in the summary.

content_id.description: The ID of the Confluence page or blog post to retrieve images from. Example: '123456789'

tools.name: confluence_get_page_restrictions
tools.description:
Get view and edit restrictions for a Confluence page.

Returns the current restriction lists for the read (view) and update (edit)
operations.  An empty list means the page is unrestricted for that operation.

page_id.description: The ID of the page

tools.name: confluence_get_page_template
tools.description: Get a Cloud page template by ID, including its storage-format body.

template_id.description: The ID of the template to retrieve.

tools.name: confluence_get_page_views
tools.description:
Get view statistics for a Confluence page.

Note: This tool is only available for Confluence Cloud. Server/Data Center
instances do not support the Analytics API.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'.

include_title.description: Whether to fetch and include the page title

tools.name: confluence_get_space_page_tree
tools.description:
Get page hierarchy for a Confluence space as a flat list.

Returns pages with parent_id and depth attributes for token-efficient
processing. Filter by depth to focus on relevant sections, or find
pages by title. Much more efficient than rendering full ASCII trees.

Use this to understand space organization before creating/moving pages.

limit.description: Max pages to fetch

tools.name: confluence_get_space_permissions
tools.description:
List all permission assignments for a Confluence space.

Wraps GET /wiki/api/v2/spaces/{id}/permissions.

Note: This tool is only available for Confluence Cloud. Server/Data Center
instances use different permission APIs.

Returns a JSON object with a 'results' list of permission assignment objects.
Each entry contains the principal (user or group), the operation permitted,
and the target. Use this to audit who has access to a space.

space_id.description: Numeric ID of the Confluence space. This is the internal space ID, not the space key. Example: '98304'. You can find the space ID from the Confluence REST API (GET /wiki/api/v2/spaces) or from the space URL.

limit.description: Maximum number of permission entries to return. Defaults to 25.

cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor from a previous response.

tools.name: confluence_list_page_templates
tools.description:
List Confluence page content templates.

This operation is only available for Confluence Cloud.
Returns template metadata (ID, name, description, type) without the
full body.  Use confluence_get_page_template to fetch a template's body.

space_key.description: Optional space key to list templates defined in that space. When omitted, global templates are returned.

limit.description: Maximum number of templates to return.

tools.name: confluence_move_page
tools.description: Move a Confluence page to a new parent or space.

page_id.description: ID of the page to move

target_parent_id.description: Target parent page ID. If omitted with target_space_key, moves to space root.

target_space_key.description: Target space key for cross-space moves

position.description: Position: 'append' (default, move as child of target), 'above' (move before target as sibling), or 'below' (move after target as sibling)

tools.name: confluence_reply_to_comment
tools.description: Reply to an existing comment thread on a Confluence page.

comment_id.description: The ID of the parent comment to reply to

body.description: The reply content in Markdown format

tools.name: confluence_search
tools.description: Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

limit.description: Maximum number of results (1-50)

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

tools.name: confluence_search_user
tools.description: Search Confluence users using CQL (Cloud) or group member API (Server/DC).

query.description:
Search query - a CQL query string for user search. Examples of CQL:
- Basic user lookup by full name: 'user.fullname ~ "First Last"'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

limit.description: Maximum number of results (1-50)

group_name.description: Group to search within on Server/DC instances (default: 'confluence-users'). Ignored on Cloud.

tools.name: confluence_set_page_restrictions
tools.description:
Set view and edit restrictions on a Confluence page.

Replaces all existing restrictions with the provided lists.  Omitting all
parameters (or passing empty lists) removes all restrictions.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to restrict

read_users.description: (Optional) Account IDs (Cloud) or usernames (Server/DC) allowed to view the page. Empty list = unrestricted.

read_groups.description: (Optional) Group names allowed to view the page.

edit_users.description: (Optional) Account IDs (Cloud) or usernames (Server/DC) allowed to edit the page.

edit_groups.description: (Optional) Group names allowed to edit the page.

tools.name: confluence_update_page
tools.description: Update an existing Confluence page.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to update

title.description: The new title of the page

content.description: The new content of the page. Format depends on content_format parameter and may be Markdown (default), wiki markup, storage format, or XHTML storage format. Either 'content' or 'content_file' must be provided, but not both.

is_minor_edit.description: Whether this is a minor edit

parent_id.description: Optional the new parent page ID

content_format.description: (Optional) The format of the content parameter. Options: 'markdown' (default), 'wiki', 'storage', or 'xhtml'. Use 'xhtml' when providing Confluence XHTML storage format (same as 'storage'). Wiki format uses Confluence wiki markup syntax

enable_heading_anchors.description: (Optional) Whether to enable automatic heading anchor generation. Only applies when content_format is 'markdown'

include_content.description: (Optional) Whether to include page content in the response. Defaults to false since callers already have the content at update time

emoji.description: (Optional) Page title emoji (icon shown in navigation). Can be any emoji character like '📝', '🚀', '📚'. Set to null/None to remove.

content_file.description: (Optional) Absolute or relative filesystem path to read the new page body from (UTF-8). Use this instead of 'content' when the body is too large to pass comfortably as a tool argument. Mutually exclusive with 'content'.

page_width.description: (Optional) Page layout width. Options: 'full-width', 'default'. Defaults to null (preserve existing).

table_layout.description: (Optional) Table width preset applied to all markdown tables. Options: 'full-width' (1800 px), 'wide' (960 px), 'default' (760 px). Only applies when content_format is 'markdown'.

tools.name: confluence_update_page_section
tools.description:
Update a single section of a Confluence page without affecting the rest.

Replaces only the content beneath a named heading, leaving all other
sections, macros, layouts, and Confluence-specific elements completely
intact. This avoids the data loss that occurs when a full page is
downloaded as Markdown, edited, and re-uploaded.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to update

heading_text.description: Exact text of the heading that starts the section to replace. Matching is case-sensitive. Use confluence_get_page with convert_to_markdown=false to inspect exact heading text when unsure.

new_content.description: Replacement content for the section body. Do NOT include the heading itself — only the body beneath it. Format is controlled by content_format.

content_format.description: (Optional) Format of new_content. Options: 'markdown' (default) or 'storage' (raw Confluence storage XML). Use 'storage' to insert macros or elements that markdown cannot express.

is_minor_edit.description: Whether this is a minor edit

tools.name: confluence_upload_attachment
tools.description:
Upload an attachment to Confluence content (page or blog post).

Provide the file either as a server-readable path ('file_path') or as
base64-encoded content ('content_base64' together with 'filename'). The
base64 form is intended for remote or containerized servers that cannot
read host file paths. Exactly one of the two must be supplied.

If the attachment already exists (same filename), a new version is created.
This is useful for:
- Attaching documents, images, or files to a page
- Updating existing attachments with new versions
- Adding supporting materials to documentation

content_id.description: The ID of the Confluence content (page or blog post) to attach the file to. Page IDs can be found in the page URL or by using the search/get_page tools. Example: '123456789'

file_path.description: Full path to the file to upload. Can be absolute (e.g., '/home/user/document.pdf' or 'C:\Users\name\file.docx') or relative to the current working directory (e.g., './uploads/document.pdf'). If a file with the same name already exists, a new version will be created. Requires the server to be able to read the path; for remote or containerized servers use 'content_base64' instead. Provide either 'file_path' or 'content_base64', not both.

content_base64.description: (Optional) Base64-encoded file content to upload directly, without the server reading from disk. Use this when the server cannot access host file paths (e.g. a remote or containerized MCP server). Requires 'filename'. Provide either 'file_path' or 'content_base64', not both.

filename.description: (Optional) Attachment filename, including extension (e.g. 'report.pdf'). Required when using 'content_base64'; it determines the attachment title and file type. Ignored when 'file_path' is used.

comment.description: (Optional) A comment describing this attachment or version. Visible in the attachment history. Example: 'Updated Q4 2024 figures'

minor_edit.description: (Optional) Whether this is a minor edit. If true, watchers are not notified. Default is false.

tools.name: confluence_upload_attachments
tools.description:
Upload multiple attachments to Confluence content in a single operation.

More efficient than calling upload_attachment multiple times. If files with the
same names exist, new versions are created automatically.

Useful for:
- Bulk uploading documentation assets (diagrams, screenshots, etc.)
- Adding multiple related files to a page at once
- Batch updating existing attachments with new versions

content_id.description: The ID of the Confluence content (page or blog post) to attach files to. Example: '123456789'. If uploading multiple files with the same names, new versions will be created automatically.

file_paths.description: Comma-separated list of file paths to upload. Can be absolute or relative paths. Examples: './file1.pdf,./file2.png' or 'C:\docs\report.docx,D:\image.jpg'. All files uploaded with same comment/minor_edit settings.

comment.description: (Optional) Comment for all uploaded attachments. Visible in version history. Example: 'Q4 2024 batch upload'

minor_edit.description: (Optional) Whether this is a minor edit. If true, watchers are not notified. Default is false.

tools.name: jira_add_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a Jira issue.

public.description: (Optional) For JSM/Service Desk issues only. Set to true for customer-visible comment, false for internal agent-only comment. Posted via the ServiceDesk API as a raw string; Jira Cloud renders it server-side and stores ADF (markdown observed to render on Cloud, without the client-side markdown-to-ADF guarantees of the regular comment path). Cannot be combined with visibility. If the issue's project is listed in JIRA_INTERNAL_ONLY_PROJECTS, only public=false is accepted — public=true or omitting this field is rejected.

tools.name: jira_add_worklog
tools.description: Add a worklog entry to a Jira issue.

time_spent.description: Time spent in Jira format. Examples: '1h 30m' (1 hour and 30 minutes), '1d' (1 day), '30m' (30 minutes), '4h' (4 hours)

comment.description: (Optional) Comment for the worklog in Markdown format

started.description: (Optional) Start time in ISO format. If not provided, the current time will be used. Example: '2023-08-01T12:00:00.000+0000'

original_estimate.description: (Optional) New value for the original estimate

remaining_estimate.description: (Optional) New value for the remaining estimate

tools.name: jira_assign_issue
tools.description:
Assign a Jira issue to a user using the dedicated assignment endpoint.

This is more reliable than setting assignee via update_issue, which is
silently ignored by some Jira configurations. Uses PUT /issue/{key}/assignee.

assignee.description: User identifier to assign (email, display name, or account ID), or a JSON object string from jira_search_assignable_users. Pass null or empty string to unassign the issue.

tools.name: jira_batch_create_issues
tools.description: Create multiple Jira issues in a batch.

issues.description:
JSON array of issue objects. Each object should contain:
- project_key (required): The project key (e.g., 'PROJ')
- summary (required): Issue summary/title
- issue_type (required): Type of issue (e.g., 'Task', 'Bug')
- description (optional): Issue description in Markdown format
- assignee (optional): Assignee username or email
- components (optional): Array of component names
Example: [
  {"project_key": "PROJ", "summary": "Issue 1", "issue_type": "Task"},
  {"project_key": "PROJ", "summary": "Issue 2", "issue_type": "Bug", "components": ["Frontend"]}
]

validate_only.description: If true, only validates the issues without creating them

tools.name: jira_batch_create_versions
tools.description: Batch create multiple versions in a Jira project.

versions.description:
JSON array of version objects. Each object should contain:
- name (required): Name of the version
- startDate (optional): Start date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- releaseDate (optional): Release date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- description (optional): Description of the version
Example: [
  {"name": "v1.0", "startDate": "2025-01-01", "releaseDate": "2025-02-01", "description": "First release"},
  {"name": "v2.0"}
]

tools.name: jira_batch_get_changelogs
tools.description: Get changelogs for multiple Jira issues (Cloud only).

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to filter changelogs by (e.g. 'status,assignee'). Default to None for all fields.

limit.description: Maximum number of changelogs to return in result for each issue. Default to -1 for all changelogs. Notice that it only limits the results in the response, the function will still fetch all the data.

request_participants.description: (Optional) JSON array string or comma-separated list of request participants. Examples: ["user1","user2"] or "user1,user2"

attachments.description: (Optional) JSON array string of files to attach to the created request. Each object must contain 'filename', 'mime_type', and base64-encoded 'base64' content. Example: [{"filename": "log.txt", "mime_type": "text/plain", "base64": "aGVsbG8="}]

strict_on_behalf.description: If true, fail immediately when raiseOnBehalfOf cannot be applied. If false, retry without raiseOnBehalfOf and return a fallback warning.

tools.name: jira_download_attachments
tools.description:
Download attachments from a Jira issue.

Returns attachment contents as base64-encoded content so that they are
available over the MCP protocol without requiring filesystem access on
the server. Image attachments are returned as ``EmbeddedResource`` blobs;
all other attachments (documents, archives, etc.) are returned as
``TextContent`` carrying a base64 payload, since many MCP clients only
forward ``EmbeddedResource`` blobs for recognized image MIME types and
otherwise drop the attachment (#1419).

Returns all fields (required and optional) for the given project and

their schema. Use jira_get_field_options when a returned field needs its

tools.name: jira_get_cross_project_dependencies

Find all cross-project issue links for a project.

Scans issues in the project, extracts every issue link whose

tools.name: jira_get_field_options
tools.description:
Get allowed option values for a custom field.

Returns the list of valid options for select, multi-select, radio,
checkbox, and cascading select custom fields.

Cloud: Uses the Field Context Option API. If context_id is not provided,
automatically resolves to the global context.

Server/DC: Uses createmeta to get allowedValues. Requires project_key
and issue_type parameters.

field_id.description: Custom field ID (e.g., 'customfield_10001'). Use jira_search_fields to find field IDs.

context_id.description: Field context ID (Cloud only). If omitted, auto-resolves to the global context.

issue_type.description: Issue type name (required for Server/DC). Example: 'Bug'

contains.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on option values. Also matches child values in cascading selects.

return_limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (applied after filtering).

values_only.description: If true, return only value strings in a compact JSON format instead of full option objects.

tools.name: jira_get_issue
tools.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue.

Includes Epic links and relationship information. Use the
``include`` parameter to inline enrichments (remote_links,
transitions, watchers, changelog, comments, worklogs) so that
separate tool calls are not needed.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

include.description: (Optional) Comma-separated sections to inline in the response, avoiding extra tool calls. Supported: all, remote_links, transitions, watchers, changelog, comments, worklogs

use_display_names.description: When true, custom field keys in the output use human-readable display names (e.g. 'Story Points') instead of opaque IDs (e.g. 'customfield_10243'). The 'names' expansion is added automatically. Standard fields are unaffected.

tools.name: jira_get_issue_sla
tools.description:
Calculate SLA metrics for a Jira issue.

Computes various time-based metrics including cycle time, lead time,
time spent in each status, due date compliance, and more.

Working hours can be configured via environment variables:
- JIRA_SLA_WORKING_HOURS_ONLY: Enable working hours filtering (true/false)
- JIRA_SLA_WORKING_HOURS_START: Start time (e.g., "09:00")
- JIRA_SLA_WORKING_HOURS_END: End time (e.g., "17:00")
- JIRA_SLA_WORKING_DAYS: Working days (e.g., "1,2,3,4,5" for Mon-Fri)
- JIRA_SLA_TIMEZONE: Timezone for calculations (e.g., "America/New_York")

metrics.description: Comma-separated list of SLA metrics to calculate. Available: cycle_time, lead_time, time_in_status, due_date_compliance, resolution_time, first_response_time. Defaults to configured metrics or 'cycle_time,time_in_status'.

working_hours_only.description: Calculate using working hours only (excludes weekends/non-business hours). Defaults to value from JIRA_SLA_WORKING_HOURS_ONLY environment variable.

include_raw_dates.description: Include raw date values in the response

fields.description: JSON string of fields to update. For 'assignee', provide a string identifier (email, name, or accountId). For 'description', provide text in Markdown format; on Jira Cloud, use '{expand:Title}...{expand}' for a collapsible section. Defaults to '*all' (the complete issue, which can be very large). TOKEN-SAVING TIP: after an update you usually do NOT need the whole issue back. Pass a comma-separated list of just the field(s) you care about (e.g., 'summary,duedate'), or a single light field such as 'status' for a minimal confirmation - this can cut the response by thousands of tokens. The issue 'key' is always returned regardless. If you later need other fields, fetch them on demand with jira_get_issue (which also supports field filtering). Use '*all' only when you genuinely need the full updated issue.

tools.name: jira_update_proforma_form_answers
tools.description:
Update form field answers using the Jira Forms REST API.

This is the primary method for updating form data. Each answer object
must specify the question ID, answer type, and value.

**⚠️ KNOWN LIMITATION - DATETIME fields:**
The Jira Forms API does NOT properly preserve time components in DATETIME fields.
Only the date portion is stored; times are reset to midnight (00:00:00).

**Workaround for DATETIME fields:**
Use jira_update_issue to directly update the underlying custom fields instead:
1. Get the custom field ID from the form details (question's "jiraField" property)
2. Use jira_update_issue with fields like: {"customfield_XXXXX": "2026-01-09T11:50:00-08:00"}

Example:
```python
# Instead of updating via form (loses time):
# jira_update_proforma_form_answers(issue_key, form_id, [{"questionId": "91", "type": "DATETIME", "value": "..."}])

# Use direct field update (preserves time):
jira_update_issue(issue_key, {"customfield_10542": "2026-01-09T11:50:00-08:00"})
```

**Automatic DateTime Conversion:**
For DATE and DATETIME fields, you can provide values as:
- ISO 8601 strings (e.g., "2024-12-17T19:00:00Z", "2024-12-17")
- Unix timestamps in milliseconds (e.g., 1734465600000)

The tool automatically converts ISO 8601 strings to Unix timestamps.

Example answers:
[
    {"questionId": "q1", "type": "TEXT", "value": "Updated description"},
    {"questionId": "q2", "type": "SELECT", "value": "Product A"},
    {"questionId": "q3", "type": "NUMBER", "value": 42},
    {"questionId": "q4", "type": "DATE", "value": "2024-12-17"}

tools.name: advsec_get_alerts
tools.description: Retrieve Advanced Security alerts for a repository. Results are scoped to the specified project and repository. Branch filters (onlyDefaultBranch, ref) apply only to code, dependency, and license alerts; they are not applicable to secret alerts and are ignored by the service, so they neither include nor exclude secrets. To narrow secret alerts by confidence, pass a single 'confidenceLevels' value ('High' or 'Other'); selecting every level is treated as no confidence filter.

ref.description: Filter non-secret alerts by git reference (branch), e.g. 'refs/heads/main'. When omitted and onlyDefaultBranch is true, only alerts on the default branch are returned. Not applicable to secret alerts and ignored by this tool when alertType is 'Secret'. When alertType is unspecified, this filter is still sent and may exclude secret alerts from the results; query alertType 'Secret' separately to retrieve all secrets.

onlyDefaultBranch.description: For non-secret alerts: if true (the service default when omitted) only return alerts found on the default branch; if false, return alerts from all branches. Ignored when 'ref' is provided. Not applicable to secret alerts and ignored by this tool when alertType is 'Secret'. When alertType is unspecified, this filter is still sent and may exclude secret alerts from the results; query alertType 'Secret' separately to retrieve all secrets.

confidenceLevels.description: Only applicable to secret alerts. Accepted values are 'High' and 'Other'. Pass a single value (e.g. ['High']) to narrow secrets to that confidence level. Leave unset to return secrets without a confidence filter. Do not select both levels to widen results: the Alerts service does not accept a multi-value confidence filter and would return no alerts, so this tool treats an all-levels selection as no filter and omits it.

validity.description: Only applicable to secret alerts. If omitted, alerts of all validity statuses are returned (no validity filter is applied). Filtering by validity may return fewer alerts than 'top'; use the continuation token to fetch any remaining alerts.

tools.name: wiki_upsert_page
tools.description: Create or update a wiki page with content.

wikiIdentifier.description: The unique identifier or name of the wiki.

path.description: The path of the wiki page (e.g., '/Home' or '/Documentation/Setup').

content.description: The content of the wiki page in markdown format.

project.description: The project name or ID where the wiki is located. If not provided, the default project will be used.

etag.description: ETag for editing existing pages (optional, will be fetched if not provided).

branch.description: The branch name for the wiki repository. Defaults to 'wikiMaster' which is the default branch for Azure DevOps wikis.

tools.name: wit_backlog
tools.description: Retrieve backlog data for a project and team. Use the action parameter to specify the operation.

action.description: The action to perform. Options: list (list backlog levels for a team), list_work_items (list work items in a specific backlog level), reorder (move work items to a new position in a backlog or iteration).

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a team selection prompt will be shown.

backlogId.description: The ID of the backlog category to retrieve work items from. Required for: list_work_items.

ids.description: The IDs of the work items to reorder. Required for: reorder.

previousId.description: The ID of the work item that should be before the reordered items. Use 0 to specify the beginning of the list. Optional for: reorder.

nextId.description: The ID of the work item that should be after the reordered items. Use 0 to specify the end of the list. Optional for: reorder.

parentId.description: The parent ID for all work items involved in the operation. Use 0 to indicate the items have no parent. Optional for: reorder.

iterationPath.description: The iteration path for the reorder operation. Used when reordering items in an iteration backlog. Optional for: reorder.

iterationId.description: The iteration ID. When provided, reorder items in that iteration instead of the team backlog. Used for: reorder.

tools.name: wit_query
tools.description: Retrieve work item query data for a project. Use the action parameter to specify the operation.

action.description: The action to perform. Options: get (get a query by ID or path), get_results (run a saved query and return results), wiql (execute an ad-hoc WIQL query).

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

query.description: The ID or path of the query. Required for: get.

expand.description: Expand parameter to include additional details. Used for: get.

depth.description: Depth of expansion. Used for: get. Defaults to 0.

includeDeleted.description: Include deleted items. Used for: get. Defaults to false.

useIsoDateFormat.description: Use ISO date format in the response. Used for: get. Defaults to false.

id.description: The ID of the saved query. Required for: get_results.

team.description: Team name or ID. Used for: get_results, wiql.

timePrecision.description: Include time precision in date fields. Used for: get_results, wiql.

top.description: Maximum number of results to return. Used for: get_results, wiql. Defaults to 50.

responseType.description: Response type: 'full' returns complete results (default), 'ids' returns only work item IDs. Used for: get_results.

wiql.description: The WIQL query string to execute. Required for: wiql. Example: "SELECT [System.Id] FROM WorkItems WHERE [System.TeamProject] = @project".

tools.name: wit_work_item
tools.description: Retrieve work item data for a project. Use the action parameter to specify the operation.

action.description: The action to perform. Options: get (get a single work item by ID), get_batch (get multiple work items by IDs), list_comments (list comments on a work item), my (get work items relevant to the authenticated user), list_revisions (list revisions of a work item), list_for_iteration (list work items for a team iteration), get_type (get metadata for a work item type).

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

id.description: Work item ID. Required for: get.

ids.description: Work item IDs. Required for: get_batch.

workItemId.description: Work item ID. Required for: list_comments, list_revisions.

fields.description: Field names to include in the response. Used for: get, get_batch. For get, cannot be combined with expand.

asOf.description: Retrieve the work item as of a specific date. Used for: get.

expand.description: Expand options (None, Fields, Relations, Links, All). Used for: get, list_revisions. For get, cannot be combined with fields.

top.description: Maximum number of results to return. Used for: list_comments, my, list_revisions. Defaults vary by action.

includeCompleted.description: Include completed work items. Used for: my. Defaults to false.

type.description: Type of work items to retrieve. Used for: my. Defaults to 'assignedtome'.

skip.description: Number of results to skip for pagination. Used for: list_revisions.

team.description: Team name or ID. Used for: list_for_iteration.

workItemType.description: Work item type name. Required for: get_type.

tools.name: wit_work_item_attachment
tools.description: Download a work item attachment by its ID. By default returns the content as a base64-encoded resource. If savePath is provided, saves the file locally to that directory and returns the file path instead. Useful for viewing images (e.g. screenshots) or other files attached to work items such as bugs. If a project is not specified, you will be prompted to select one.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

attachmentId.description: The GUID of the attachment. Found in the attachment URL: https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_apis/wit/attachments/{attachmentId}

fileName.description: The file name of the attachment, e.g. 'screenshot.png'. Used to determine the MIME type or the saved file's name.

savePath.description: Optional local directory path where the file should be saved. Must be a relative path (e.g. 'temp' or 'downloads/attachments'); absolute paths and path traversals are not allowed. If provided, saves the attachment to this directory and returns the file path. If omitted, returns the content as a base64-encoded resource.

tools.name: wit_work_item_comment_write
tools.description: Write operations for work item comments. Use the action parameter to specify the operation.

action.description: The action to perform. Options: add (add a comment to a work item), update (update an existing comment on a work item).

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

workItemId.description: The ID of the work item. Required for: add, update.

text.description: The comment text. Required for: add, update.

commentId.description: The ID of the comment to update. Required for: update.

format.description: Format of the comment text. Optional, defaults to 'Markdown'.

tools.name: wit_work_item_link_write
tools.description: Write operations for work item links. Use the action parameter to specify the operation.

action.description: The action to perform. Options: link (link two work items together), unlink (remove links from a work item), link_to_pull_request (link a work item to a pull request), add_artifact_link (add a repository, branch, commit, or build artifact link to a work item).

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

id.description: The ID of the work item to update.

linkToId.description: The ID of the work item to link to. Required unless type is 'hyperlink'.

url.description: The URL for a hyperlink. Required when type is 'hyperlink'.

updates.description: Link operations to apply. Required for: link.

id.description: Work item ID to remove links from. Required for: unlink.

type.description: Link type to remove. Required for: unlink.

url.description: URL to match when removing a link. Used for: unlink. If not provided, all links of the specified type are removed.

projectId.description: The project ID (GUID). Required for: link_to_pull_request, and add_artifact_link (Git/Wiki types).

repositoryId.description: The repository ID. Required for: link_to_pull_request and add_artifact_link (Git types).

pullRequestId.description: The pull request ID. Required for: link_to_pull_request; used for: add_artifact_link (Pull Request type).

workItemId.description: The work item ID. Required for: link_to_pull_request, add_artifact_link.

pullRequestProjectId.description: Project ID containing the pull request. Used for: link_to_pull_request. Defaults to projectId.

artifactUri.description: The complete VSTFS URI of the artifact. Used for: add_artifact_link. If provided, individual component parameters are ignored.

branchName.description: The branch name. Used for: add_artifact_link (Branch type).

commitId.description: The commit SHA hash. Used for: add_artifact_link (Fixed in Commit type).

buildId.description: The build ID. Used for: add_artifact_link (Build, Found in build, Integrated in build types).

wikiId.description: The wiki ID (GUID). Used for: add_artifact_link (Wiki type).

pageId.description: The numeric wiki page ID. Used for: add_artifact_link (Wiki type). Takes precedence over pagePath.

pagePath.description: The full wiki page path. Used for: add_artifact_link (Wiki type) when pageId is not provided.

linkType.description: Type of artifact link. Used for: add_artifact_link. Defaults to 'Branch'.

comment.description: Comment to include with the artifact link. Used for: add_artifact_link.

tools.name: wit_work_item_write
tools.description: Write operations for work items. Use the action parameter to specify the operation.

action.description: The action to perform. Options: create (create a new work item), update (update fields on a single work item), update_batch (update multiple work items in one call), add_child (create child work items under a parent).

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

id.description: Work item ID to update. Required for: update.

workItemType.description: The type of work item. Required for: create, add_child.

format.description: Format for large text fields. Optional.

fields.description: Field values to set on the work item. Required for: create.

op.description: The operation to perform. Use 'test' with path '/rev' to enforce optimistic concurrency.

path.description: The path to operate on, e.g. '/fields/System.Title' or '/rev' for a revision test.

value.description: The operation value. Required for add, replace, and test; omit for remove. For a test on '/rev', pass the numeric revision previously read.

updates.description: Field updates for a single work item. Required for: update. For a safe read-modify-write, prepend a test operation on "/rev" with value set to the numeric revision returned by the preceding read; Azure DevOps rejects the entire update if the current revision differs.

id.description: The work item ID to update.

path.description: The field path, e.g. '/fields/System.Title'.

value.description: The new value for the field.

format.description: Format for large text fields. Optional.

batchUpdates.description: Updates for multiple work items. Required for: update_batch.

parentId.description: The ID of the parent work item. Required for: add_child.

title.description: The title of the child work item.

description.description: The description of the child work item.

format.description: Format for the description. Defaults to 'Markdown'.

areaPath.description: Optional area path for the child work item.

iterationPath.description: Optional iteration path for the child work item.

items.description: Child work items to create. Required for: add_child.

tools.name: work
tools.description: Retrieve work-related data for a project or team. Use the action parameter to specify the operation.

action.description: The action to perform. Options: list_iterations (list all iterations in a project), list_team_iterations (list iterations assigned to a team), get_team_settings (get team settings including default iteration and area path), get_team_capacity (get team capacity for an iteration), get_iteration_capacities (get capacity for all teams in an iteration).

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project. Reuse from prior context if already known. If not provided, a project selection prompt will be shown.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. Required for list_team_iterations, get_team_settings, and get_team_capacity. Reuse from prior context if already known.

iterationId.description: The Iteration ID. Required for get_team_capacity and get_iteration_capacities.

timeframe.description: The timeframe for list_team_iterations. Only 'current' is supported.

depth.description: Depth of children to fetch. Used for list_iterations. Defaults to 2.

excludedIds.description: An optional array of iteration IDs, and their children, to exclude from results. Used for list_iterations.

tools.name: work_capacity_write
tools.description: Update the team capacity of a team member for a specific iteration in a project.

action.description: The action to perform. Only 'update' is supported.

project.description: The name or Id of the Azure DevOps project.

team.description: The name or Id of the Azure DevOps team.

teamMemberId.description: The team member Id for the specific team member.

iterationId.description: The Iteration Id to update the capacity for.

capacityPerDay.description: The capacity per day for this activity.

activities.description: Array of activities and their daily capacities for the team member.

start.description: Start date of the day off in ISO format.

end.description: End date of the day off in ISO format.

daysOff.description: Array of days off for the team member, each with a start and end date in ISO format.

tools.name: work_iteration_write
tools.description: Create or assign iterations in an Azure DevOps project. Use the action parameter to specify the operation.

action.description: The action to perform. 'create' creates new iterations in the project; 'assign' assigns existing iterations to a team.

project.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps project.

team.description: The name or ID of the Azure DevOps team. Required for assign.

iterationName.description: The name of the iteration to create. Used for create.

startDate.description: The start date of the iteration in ISO format (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z'). Used for create.

finishDate.description: The finish date of the iteration in ISO format (e.g., '2023-01-31T23:59:59Z'). Used for create.

identifier.description: The identifier of the iteration to assign. Used for assign.

path.description: The path of the iteration to assign, e.g., 'Project/Iteration'. Used for assign.

iterations.description: An array of iterations to process. For create: provide iterationName and optional dates. For assign: provide identifier and path.

tools.name: brave_local_search
tools.description:
Searches for local businesses and places using Brave's Local Search API. Best for queries related to physical locations, businesses, restaurants, services, etc. Returns detailed information including:
- Business names and addresses
- Ratings and review counts
- Phone numbers and opening hours
Use this when the query implies 'near me' or mentions specific locations. Automatically falls back to web search if no local results are found.

query.description: Local search query (e.g. 'pizza near Central Park')

tools.name: brave_web_search
tools.description: Performs a web search using the Brave Search API, ideal for general queries, news, articles, and online content. Use this for broad information gathering, recent events, or when you need diverse web sources. Supports pagination, content filtering, and freshness controls. Maximum 20 results per request, with offset for pagination.

query.description: Search query (max 400 chars, 50 words)

tools.name: act
tools.description: Perform an action on the page

tools.name: end
tools.description: Close the current Browserbase session

tools.name: extract
tools.description: Extract data from the page

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a URL

tools.name: observe
tools.description: Observe actionable elements on the page

tools.name: start
tools.description: Create or reuse a Browserbase session

tools.name: click
tools.description: Clicks on the provided element

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

dblClick.description: Set to true for double clicks. Default is false.

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: close_page
tools.description: Closes the page by its index. The last open page cannot be closed.

pageId.description: The ID of the page to close. Call list_pages to list pages.

tools.name: drag
tools.description: Drag an element onto another element

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

from_uid.description: The uid of the element to drag

to_uid.description: The uid of the element to drop into

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: emulate
tools.description: Emulates various features on the target page.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

networkConditions.description: Throttle network. Omit to disable throttling.

cpuThrottlingRate.description: Represents the CPU slowdown factor. Omit or set the rate to 1 to disable throttling

geolocation.description: Geolocation (`<latitude>,<longitude>`) to emulate. Latitude between -90 and 90. Longitude between -180 and 180. Omit to clear the geolocation override.

userAgent.description: User agent to emulate. Set to empty string to clear the user agent override.

colorScheme.description: Emulate the dark or the light mode. Set to "auto" to reset to the default.

viewport.description: Emulate device viewports '<width>x<height>x<devicePixelRatio>[,mobile][,touch][,landscape]'. 'touch' and 'mobile' to emulate mobile devices. 'landscape' to emulate landscape mode.

extraHttpHeaders.description: Extra HTTP headers as a JSON string object, e.g. {"X-Custom": "value", "Authorization": "Bearer token"}. Headers are included into every HTTP request originating from the page and persist across navigations until cleared. Pass an empty string to clear all extra headers.

tools.name: evaluate_script
tools.description: Evaluate a JavaScript function inside the target page. Returns the response as JSON, so returned values have to be JSON-serializable.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

function.description:
A JavaScript function declaration to be executed by the tool in the target page.
Example without arguments: `() => document.title` or `async () => await fetch("example.com")`.
Example with arguments: `(el) => el.innerText`

args.description: An optional list of arguments to pass to the function.

items.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

filePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a file to save the script output to. If omitted, the output is returned inline.

dialogAction.description: Handle dialogs while execution. "accept", "dismiss", or string for response of window.prompt. Defaults to accept.

waitForStableDom.description: Whether to wait for the DOM to settle. Pass false if the script only reads data. Defaults to true.

tools.name: fill
tools.description: Type text into an input, text area or select an option from a <select> element.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

value.description: The value to fill in. "true" or "false" for checkboxes and toggles, "true" for radio buttons.

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: fill_form
tools.description: Fill out multiple form elements (inputs, selects, checkboxes, radios) at once. ALWAYS prefer this tool over multiple individual 'fill' or 'click' calls when interacting with forms. It is significantly faster, more reliable, and reduces turn count. Example: Fill username, password, and check "Remember Me" in one call.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of the element to fill out

value.description: Value for the element. "true" or "false" for checkboxes and toggles, "true" for radio buttons.

elements.description: Elements from snapshot to fill out.

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: get_console_message
tools.description: Gets a console message by its ID. You can get all messages by calling list_console_messages.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

msgid.description: The msgid of a console message on the page from the listed console messages

tools.name: get_css_styles
tools.description:
Retrieve matched CSS rules, inline styles, inherited styles, and cascade information for an element identified by its UID.
Use this tool to debug why specific CSS properties are applied, overridden, or conflicting. Results are paginated and return 10 rules per page by default; use pageIdx to page through the remaining rules. Requires a UID from take_snapshot.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of the element on the page from the page content snapshot to inspect CSS styles for

pageSize.description: Maximum number of CSS rules to return per page. Defaults to 10.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). Defaults to 0 (the first page).

tools.name: get_network_request
tools.description: Gets a network request by an optional reqid, if omitted returns the currently selected request in the DevTools Network panel. Useful for inspecting request headers (including 'Cookie') and response headers (including 'Set-Cookie' and directives).

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

reqid.description: The reqid of the network request. If omitted returns the currently selected request in the DevTools Network panel.

requestFilePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a .network-request file to save the request body to. If omitted, the body is returned inline.

responseFilePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a .network-response file to save the response body to. If omitted, the body is returned inline.

tools.name: handle_dialog
tools.description: If a browser dialog was opened, use this command to handle it

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

action.description: Whether to dismiss or accept the dialog

promptText.description: Optional prompt text to enter into the dialog.

tools.name: hover
tools.description: Hover over the provided element

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: lighthouse_audit
tools.description: Get Lighthouse score and reports for accessibility, SEO, best practices, and agentic browsing. This excludes performance. For performance audits, run performance_start_trace

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

outputDirPath.description: Directory for reports. If omitted, uses temporary files.

tools.name: list_console_messages
tools.description: List all console messages for the target page since the last navigation.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of messages to return. When omitted, returns all messages.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). When omitted, returns the first page.

types.description: Filter messages to only return messages of the specified resource types. When omitted or empty, returns all messages.

includePreservedMessages.description: Set to true to return the preserved messages over the last 3 navigations.

includeStackTraces.description: Set to true to include the stack trace for each message when available. Increases the response size.

serviceWorkerId.description: Filter messages to only return messages of the specified service worker.

tools.name: list_network_requests
tools.description: Lists the most recent requests for the target page since the last navigation.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of requests to return. When omitted, returns all requests.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). When omitted, returns the first page.

resourceTypes.description: Filter requests to only return requests of the specified resource types. When omitted or empty, returns all requests.

includePreservedRequests.description: Set to true to return the preserved requests over the last 3 navigations.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Get a list of pages open in the browser.

tools.name: navigate_page
tools.description: Go to a URL, or back, forward, or reload. Use project URL if not specified otherwise.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

type.description: Navigate the page by URL, back or forward in history, or reload.

url.description: Target URL (only type=url)

ignoreCache.description: Whether to ignore cache on reload.

handleBeforeUnload.description: Whether to auto accept or beforeunload dialogs triggered by this navigation. Default is accept.

initScript.description: A JavaScript script to be executed on each new document before any other scripts for the next navigation.

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

tools.name: new_page
tools.description: Open a new tab and load a URL. Use project URL if not specified otherwise.

url.description: URL to load in a new page.

background.description: Whether to open the page in the background without bringing it to the front. Default is false (foreground).

isolatedContext.description: If specified, the page is created in an isolated browser context with the given name. Pages in the same browser context share cookies and storage. Pages in different browser contexts are fully isolated (useful for clean-slate testing of cookies and authentication).

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

tools.name: performance_analyze_insight
tools.description: Provides more detailed information on a specific Performance Insight of an insight set that was highlighted in the results of a trace recording.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

insightSetId.description: The id for the specific insight set. Only use the ids given in the "Available insight sets" list.

insightName.description: The name of the Insight you want more information on. For example: "DocumentLatency" or "LCPBreakdown"

tools.name: performance_start_trace
tools.description: Start a performance trace on the target webpage. Use to find frontend performance issues, Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS), and improve page load speed.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

reload.description: Determines if, once tracing has started, the target page should be automatically reloaded. Navigate the page to the right URL using the navigate_page tool BEFORE starting the trace if reload or autoStop is set to true.

autoStop.description: Determines if the trace recording should be automatically stopped.

filePath.description: The absolute file path, or a file path relative to the current working directory, to save the raw trace data. For example, trace.json.gz (compressed) or trace.json (uncompressed).

tools.name: performance_stop_trace
tools.description: Stop the active performance trace recording on the target webpage.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

filePath.description: The absolute file path, or a file path relative to the current working directory, to save the raw trace data. For example, trace.json.gz (compressed) or trace.json (uncompressed).

tools.name: press_key
tools.description: Press a key or key combination. Use this when other input methods like fill() cannot be used (e.g., keyboard shortcuts, navigation keys, or special key combinations).

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

key.description: A key or a combination (e.g., "Enter", "Control+A", "Control++", "Control+Shift+R"). Modifiers: Control, Shift, Alt, Meta

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: resize_page
tools.description: Resizes the page's window so that the page has specified dimension

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

tools.name: select_page
tools.description: Select a page as a context for future tool calls.

pageId.description: The ID of the page to select. Call list_pages to get available pages.

bringToFront.description: Whether to focus the page and bring it to the top.

tools.name: take_heapsnapshot
tools.description: Capture a heap snapshot of the target page. Use to analyze the memory distribution of JavaScript objects and debug memory leaks.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

filePath.description: A path to a .heapsnapshot file to save the heapsnapshot to.

tools.name: take_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the page or element.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

format.description: Type of format to save the screenshot as. Default is "png"

quality.description: Compression quality for JPEG and WebP formats (0-100). Higher values mean better quality but larger file sizes. Ignored for PNG format.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot. If omitted, takes a page screenshot.

fullPage.description: If set to true takes a screenshot of the full page instead of the currently visible viewport. Incompatible with uid.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the screenshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

tools.name: take_snapshot
tools.description:
Take a text snapshot of the target page based on the a11y tree. The snapshot lists page elements along with a unique
identifier (uid). Always use the latest snapshot. Prefer taking a snapshot over taking a screenshot. The snapshot indicates the element selected
in the DevTools Elements panel (if any).

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

verbose.description: Whether to include all possible information available in the full a11y tree. Default is false.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the snapshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

tools.name: type_text
tools.description: Type text using keyboard into a previously focused input

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

submitKey.description: Optional key to press after typing. E.g., "Enter", "Tab", "Escape"

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Upload a file through a provided element.

tools.name: list_component_versions
tools.description:
This tool lists all versions for a CircleCI component. It guides you through a multi-step process to gather the required information and provides lists of available options when parameters are missing.

     **Initial Requirements:**
     - You need either a `projectSlug` (from `listFollowedProjects`) or a `projectID`. The tool will automatically resolve the `orgID` from either of these.

     **Typical Flow:**
     1. **Start:** User requests component versions or deployment information.
     2. **Project Information:** Provide either `projectSlug` or `projectID`. The tool will automatically resolve the `orgID` and `projectID` as needed.
     3. **Environment Selection:** If `environmentID` is not provided, the tool will list all available environments for the organization and prompt the user to select one. Always return all available values without categorizing them.
     4. **Component Selection:** If `componentID` is not provided, the tool will list all available components for the project and prompt the user to select one. Always return all available values without categorizing them.
     5. **Version Listing:** Once both `environmentID` and `componentID` are provided, the tool will list all versions for that component in the specified environment.
     6. **Selection:** User selects a version from the list for subsequent operations.

     **Parameters:**
     - `projectSlug` (optional): The project slug from `listFollowedProjects` (e.g., "gh/organization/project"). Either this or `projectID` must be provided.
     - `projectID` (optional): The CircleCI project ID (UUID). Either this or `projectSlug` must be provided.
     - `orgID` (optional): The organization ID. If not provided, it will be automatically resolved from `projectSlug` or `projectID`.
     - `environmentID` (optional): The environment ID. If not provided, available environments will be listed.
     - `componentID` (optional): The component ID. If not provided, available components will be listed.

     **Behavior:**
     - The tool will guide you through the selection process step by step.
     - Automatically resolves `orgID` from `projectSlug` or `projectID` when needed.
     - When `environmentID` is missing, it lists environments and waits for user selection.
     - When `componentID` is missing (but `environmentID` is provided), it lists components and waits for user selection.
     - Only when both `environmentID` and `componentID` are provided will it list the actual component versions.
     - Make multiple calls to this tool as you gather the required parameters.

     **Common Use Cases:**
     - Identify which versions were deployed for a component
     - Identify which versions are live for a component
     - Identify which versions were deployed to an environment for a component
     - Identify which versions are not live for a component in an environment
     - Select a version for rollback or deployment operations
     - Obtain version name, namespace, and environment details for other CircleCI tools

     **Returns:**
     - When missing `environmentID`: A list of available environments with their IDs
     - When missing `componentID`: A list of available components with their IDs
